messages.content: What's the deadline for my grocery store to file its annual tax returns?

If your business has been operating for more than 18 months, you need to file your annual returns within 6 months after the end of your accounting year. For newly incorporated companies, the deadline is within 18 months of incorporation or 6 months after the first accounting period, whichever comes first. If a company stops trading permanently, it must file within 6 months of ceasing operations. Confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.

My dad's salon business in Ibadan might be paying a supplier some money for beauty supplies. How much should we pay out if we don't have to deduct withholding tax? We've heard that tax deductions can be tricky.

If your business is considered a small company (check if you meet the criteria with FIRS or a licensed accountant to confirm the definition), you don't need to deduct withholding tax on supplier payments that don't exceed NGN 2,000,000. Also, the supplier must have a valid Tax Identification Number (TIN). Always confirm any tax-related specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing, as tax rules can change and individual circumstances apply.
What's the standard VAT rate for my electronics shop in Kano and can I claim input VAT credit on all my purchases now?

The standard VAT rate is expected to remain at 7.5%. Under the new rules, businesses are also expected to be able to claim input VAT credit on most purchases, not just goods for resale or production. Confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
Do I need a TIN since I only send money home occasionally and won't be conducting any business activities in Nigeria?

You're expected to have a Tax Identification Number (TIN) only if you're liable for paying tax in Nigeria. Since you only send money home occasionally and won't be engaged in business activities in Nigeria, that's unlikely to apply. But to be sure, this is something you should confirm with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure you're in compliance with the new tax rules.
Does our grocery store in Abuja need to pay the new Development Levy and how does it work?

The Development Levy is 4% of the assessable profits of companies chargeable to tax. This levy is imposed on the assessable profits of companies like yours, but small companies and non-resident companies are exempt. Under the new rules, this levy is expected to consolidate and replace some former taxes. To confirm if your business qualifies as a small company and to understand how this applies to your specific situation, please check with the FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
What's the deadline for submitting my electronics retailer's annual tax return in Lagos?

If my shop has been in business for over 18 months, I need to file the annual return within 6 months of the end of our accounting year. For a new business, it's within 18 months of registration or 6 months after the first accounting period - whichever is earlier. And if I'm shutting down, it's 6 months from the day we stop trading.
I just moved abroad for work, how do I know if I'm still considered a Nigerian tax resident?

Under the new rules, this is expected to depend on how many days you spend in Nigeria - if you're physically present in the country for 183 days or more within any 12-month period, you're likely to be considered a tax resident. Confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure you're meeting your tax obligations.
Sister, how much tax do our Dad's earnings from the grocery store attract per year, considering he earns from the business and has rent on our family home?

According to the new rules, Dad's personal income tax is progressive, meaning the rate depends on how much he earns. Individuals earning below NGN 800,000 per annum are exempt. If his earnings exceed this, he'll be taxed at different rates, but the top rate is 25%.

As for the rent, he can claim a relief of up to 20% of the annual rent paid, but the total cannot exceed NGN 500,000. This means he'll need to declare this rent to the tax authority and provide supporting information.

Please keep in mind that these are expected rates under the new rules, and it's always best to confirm specifics with the FIRS or consult a licensed accountant to ensure accurate compliance and filing.
How does the new Capital Gains Tax rule affect my grocery and provisions store in Lagos?

Under the new rules, this is expected to change how capital gains are taxed for businesses like yours. For companies, capital gains tax is expected to be around 30%, which is the standard CIT rate, replacing the prior flat 10% rate. For individual business owners, capital gains are expected to be taxed under the personal income tax bands, which go up to 25%, also replacing the prior flat 10% rate. However, small companies might be exempt from CGT, but it's essential to confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
Our furniture workshop in Lagos now does capital gains, what's changed since these changes to Capital Gains Tax for our type of business?

With the changes, our business will now pay a 30% effective Capital Gains Tax rate (this is expected to apply to companies under the new rules), whereas previously, the flat 10% rate applied. Additionally, individuals' capital gains will no longer be taxed separately, but instead will be included in their personal income tax. Small companies like ours might still be exempt, however.

To confirm our specific tax implications, please consult with the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing.

Hi, my dad used to handle the books but now I do, and I'm trying to understand the new tax rules - how do personal income tax bands and rent relief work for my dad as the owner of our printing and stationery bureau in Kano?

Under the new rules, personal income tax is expected to be calculated using progressive bands from 0% to 25%. This is expected to mean that individuals earning below NGN 800,000 per annum are exempt from PIT. Additionally, your dad may be eligible for rent relief, which is expected to be 20% of annual rent paid, capped at a maximum of NGN 500,000, as long as he declares annual rent and provides supporting information to the tax authority. To confirm specifics, please check with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
If I only send money home occasionally from abroad, do I need a TIN?

Under the new rules, you're expected to have a TIN only if you have taxable income or business activities in Nigeria. Since you're just sending money from abroad and not doing any business or having income here, it's unlikely you need a TIN. However, for certainty, it's best to confirm with FIRS or a licensed accountant, just to be sure you're following the rules correctly before filing.
I work abroad and send money to my family in Nigeria every month, is the salary I earn overseas taxable in Nigeria if it's paid into my Nigerian bank account?

Under the new rules, this is expected to be exempt from Nigerian tax since the income is earned entirely outside Nigeria. However, it's crucial to note that only income earned entirely outside Nigeria by a non-resident, such as from remote work for foreign employers, would qualify for this exemption, even if remitted into Nigeria. To confirm specifics and how this applies to your situation, please check with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
We're a printing and stationery bureau in Lagos, Nigeria, and our turnover is quite low. Do we have to pay Companies Income Tax (CIT) at all?

Based on our current annual gross turnover of below NGN 100,000,000 (₦100 million) and the Nigeria Tax Reform Acts 2025, it seems our business might be classified as a 'small company' which is exempt from CIT at 0%. However, we need to confirm if our total fixed assets (other than cash and debtors) are also below NGN 250,000,000 (₦250 million) to be fully exempt. It's always best to check the details with the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing any taxes to ensure accuracy and compliance.
Do I need to pay the new Development Levy for my furniture workshop in Port Harcourt?

The Development Levy is imposed on the assessable profits of companies chargeable to tax at a rate of 4%. However, small companies and non-resident companies are exempt. This is expected to consolidate and replace former taxes like the Tertiary Education Tax and the Nigeria Police Trust Fund levy into one unified levy. To confirm whether your business owes this levy, check with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing.
What has changed about paying Capital Gains Tax in Nigeria for fashion boutiques like mine? Can you break it down for me?

According to the new tax laws under the Nigeria Tax Reform Acts 2025, if your fashion boutique makes a profit from selling your business, the tax rules have changed. For individuals like you, capital gains are now taxed based on your personal income tax band, which means it could be up to 25% of the profit. That's a change from the previous flat rate of 10%. Additionally, small companies are exempt from Capital Gains Tax, but first, you need to confirm your company's classification. And companies that are not small, like yours, will be taxed at a rate of 30% or their standard Corporate Income Tax rate. As a business owner, make sure to consult with a licensed accountant or the Nigeria Revenue Service to understand your specific situation and to confirm the correct tax rate for your boutique before filing taxes.
Does my electronics retail business in Abuja owe the new Development Levy?

Your business will be subject to the Development Levy if it's not a small company or a non-resident company, and it's chargeable to tax under Chapters Two and Three of the Act. The Development Levy is 4% of the assessable profits of companies like yours. This is expected to consolidate and replace some previous taxes, like the Tertiary Education Tax and the Nigeria Police Trust Fund levy, under the new rules. Confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
Our hardware shop in Ibadan makes a lot of profit. Do we need to pay Companies Income Tax?

Based on the Nigeria Tax Reform Acts 2026, if your shop's annual gross turnover is ₦100 million or less and its total fixed assets are ₦250 million or less, then under the new rules, you are considered a 'small company' and are exempt from paying Companies Income Tax. Otherwise, you may be subject to Companies Income Tax at the standard rate of 30%.

Please confirm specifics with the FIRS (Federal Inland Revenue Service) or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure you meet all the requirements and comply with the regulations.
Do I need a Tax Identification Number (TIN) if I'm a Nigerian living abroad and just send money back home every now and then?

This is expected to depend on whether you have taxable income or business activities in Nigeria - if not, you might not need a TIN. Under the new rules, it's likely that a TIN is required only for individuals or entities with such connections to Nigeria. To confirm your specific situation, please check with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
What's the new VAT rate for our furniture workshop, and can we claim back VAT on most purchases we make?

The standard VAT rate remains 7.5% under the new rules. You can now claim input VAT credit on most purchases, not just those used for resale or production, which will help reduce your VAT expenses on supplies like lumber, tools, and furniture parts. It's good to verify these changes with FIRS or a licensed accountant, like you would with any significant change to your business finances, to ensure you're meeting all the requirements and deadlines.
Do I need to deduct withholding tax when I pay my suppliers for goods worth less than 2 million naira?

This is expected to depend on the specifics of your situation, but under the new rules, small companies like your hardware shop may not need to deduct withholding tax at source for transactions of NGN 2,000,000 or less, if your supplier has a valid Tax Identification Number. Confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
Do I need to pay Companies Income Tax as a printing and stationery bureau in Ibadan, Nigeria?

To qualify for this exemption, you need to meet BOTH criteria: first, your annual gross turnover should not exceed NGN 100,000,000 (that's ₦100 million), and second, your total fixed assets should be NGN 250,000,000 (that's ₦250 million) or below. If you meet both of these conditions, under the new rules, your printing and stationery bureau will be considered a 'small company', and thus, you won't have to pay Companies Income Tax.

Please confirm your business specifics with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing your tax returns.
I just started my electronics shop in Abuja and I'm not sure about the tax registration deadline, what happens if I don't register my business for tax on time?

If your business doesn't register for tax on time, you'll be liable for a penalty of NGN 50,000 for the first month, and then NGN 25,000 for each subsequent month. Also, if your business is awarded a contract by a statutory body or company while unregistered, they will also be liable for a penalty. Be sure to confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure compliance.
I have a job abroad and my salary gets paid into my bank account in Nigeria. Do I have to pay tax on the income?

Under the new Nigeria Tax Reform Acts 2025, it seems that any income you earn entirely outside Nigeria, even if it gets paid into a Nigerian bank account, is expected to be exempt from Nigerian tax. This applies to remote work for foreign employers as well. However, it's always best to confirm the specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant to ensure you're not missing anything and to avoid any potential tax issues when filing returns.
What's the deal with Capital Gains Tax now for my furniture workshop - did the rates really change?

Under the new rules, this is expected to change how Capital Gains Tax works for your business. For companies like yours, the Capital Gains Tax rate is expected to be 30%, which is the standard CIT rate, replacing the prior flat 10% rate. If you're a small company, you might be exempt from CGT, but for individuals, including those owning small workshops, capital gains are now taxed under the personal income tax bands, up to 25%. Confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
I've just moved abroad for work but still want to send money back home occasionally. Do I need to get a Tax Identification Number (TIN)?

You're not expected to get a TIN unless you have any taxable income or are conducting business activities in Nigeria. Since you're only sending money home occasionally and not working in Nigeria, it's unlikely you'll need one. However, this is subject to change, so please confirm the specifics with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing to avoid any issues.
I work abroad and send money home to Nigeria every month, is the salary I earn from my foreign job taxable in Nigeria?

Under the new rules, this is expected to be exempt from Nigerian tax since it's earned entirely outside Nigeria, even if you remit some of it into the country. To confirm specifics, please verify with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
Our store in Abuja still hasn't registered for tax with FIRS, and it's already been a few months. What kind of penalty can we expect? We're worried about this affecting our business.

Under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, you'll need to pay NGN 50,000 for the first month of failing to register for tax. For each subsequent month, it's an extra NGN 25,000. There's also a penalty on any statutory body or company that awards a contract to an unregistered business, but that's up to them to deal with. Just to be sure, let's confirm the specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing to avoid any issues.
What's the VAT rate I should charge my clients at the salon and can I claim back VAT on all the supplies I buy?

This is expected to be 7.5% under the new rules, and you're also expected to be able to claim input VAT credit on most of your purchases, not just the goods you resell or use for production. Check with FIRS or a licensed accountant to confirm the specifics before filing.

I need to pay a supplier for some printing equipment from our Port Harcourt store. If the bill is NGN 200,000, do we have to withhold any tax? And what about the supplier's Tax Identification Number (TIN), is that important too?

Based on the new tax rules, if your printing and stationery bureau doesn't meet the small company definition, and the payment is more than NGN 2,000,000, or your supplier doesn't have a valid Tax Identification Number (TIN), you might need to deduct withholding tax. However, under the new rules, this is expected to be the case only for high-value transactions (more than NGN 2,000,000) or suppliers without a valid TIN. This is expected to help simplify tax deductions for many small businesses like yours. Confirm all details with FIRS or a licensed accountant before making any payment.
I'm a Nigerian living abroad and I send money back home every month, will I be taxed on that money twice - once in my host country and again in Nigeria?

This is expected to be prevented under the new rules, as Nigeria has agreements with several countries, like the UK, Canada, and South Africa, to avoid double taxation. If your host country doesn't have such an agreement with Nigeria, the Act is expected to provide some relief to prevent double taxation. To confirm specifics, check with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
Will money I send home to my family in Nigeria be taxed if I'm working abroad and sending them the money for their personal expenses?

Under the new tax rules, money sent home to family for genuine personal purposes like family support, gifts, and community contributions is NOT taxable income. This is expected to be an exemption, but please confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure compliance with new regulations.
I'm a Nigerian living abroad and I work remotely for a foreign company, they pay my salary into my Nigerian bank account - do I have to pay tax on that in Nigeria?

Under the new rules, this is expected to be exempt from Nigerian tax since you earned it entirely outside Nigeria, even though it's paid into a Nigerian account. However, to confirm specifics, please check with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
If my grocery and provisions store in Port Harcourt doesn't register for tax on time, what happens?

The Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 says you'll get a fine of NGN 50,000 for the first month of failing to register. Every month after that, it's NGN 25,000. Also, any company that awards a contract to an unregistered business could get fined too.

If you're not sure what to do or want to clarify the tax registration process for your business, please confirm specifics with the FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
I'm a Nigerian living abroad, will I be taxed on the money I send back home to my family?

Under the new rules, this is expected to not be taxable as genuine personal remittances, such as family support, are not considered taxable income. Confirm specifics with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing.
If my electronics retailer in Abuja isn't registered for tax yet and it's past the deadline, what happens and how much will I have to pay?

content: If your business fails to register for tax on time, you'll face penalties. For the first month, you'll need to pay NGN 50,000.
For each subsequent month you continue to delay registration, you'll be penalized an additional NGN 25,000.
Keep in mind that business partners, like companies that award contracts to unregistered vendors, may also be held liable for these penalties.

I send money to Nigeria every month. Will I get taxed twice, once where I'm living abroad and again when it arrives in Nigeria?

If there's no DTA in place, relief is available through the new rules, but it's always best to confirm specifics with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing to make sure everything is correct.
What's the current VAT rate for my hardware shop in Ibadan and can I claim VAT credits on all purchases now?

Confirm specifics with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing.
We're switching to a new accounting system next quarter. How has Capital Gains Tax changed for my hardware shop in Port Harcourt?

Under the new rules, my CGT rate is 30% - this is expected to be effective for the standard CIT rate, not a flat 10% any more. For individuals, the tax rate is now based on personal income tax bands, up to 25%. If I'm small enough, I might be exempt. I should check with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant to confirm how this affects our specific shop's taxes, especially with the new system coming in.
I just started my electronics retail business in Kano, do I need a Tax Identification Number and how do I get one?

This is expected to be required for your business since it's based in Nigeria and has business activities. Under the new rules, individuals may be able to obtain a TIN using their National Identification Number (NIN), but for businesses like yours, it's expected that you may need to apply through the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) or the Nigeria Revenue Service if you haven't already registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC). Confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure you're meeting all the necessary requirements.
Will I be taxed for money I send home to my family or friends in Nigeria?

Under the new tax reforms, money you genuinely send home as family support, gifts, community contributions, or personal transfers is not considered taxable income. However, this is expected to be reviewed under the new rules; it's always a good idea to confirm specifics with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure compliance.
I own a small salon and beauty supplies shop in Kano, do I have to pay Companies Income Tax?

If your annual gross turnover is NGN 100,000,000 or below and your total fixed assets are NGN 250,000,000 or below, this is expected to qualify your business as a 'small company'. As a small company, you are expected to be taxed at 0%. However, it's essential to confirm your specific situation with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure you meet all the necessary criteria.
Will I be taxed on my foreign income by both the country I live in and Nigeria when I return?

This is expected to be prevented under the Nigeria Tax Reform Acts 2026. Nigeria has Double Taxation Agreements (DTAs) with several countries, which typically covers individuals working abroad. If no DTA exists with your country of residence, the Act provides unilateral relief to avoid double taxation. However, to ensure you fully understand how this affects your specific situation, please confirm these details with the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing your taxes.
Do I need to pay Companies Income Tax for our grocery and provisions store in Lagos?

If your store's annual gross turnover is NGN 100 million or below and total fixed assets are NGN 250 million or below, it is expected to be classified as a small company and pay 0% Companies Income Tax. However, if your store exceeds either of these thresholds, the standard company rate of 30% may apply. Please confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
Does my furniture workshop owe the new Development Levy in Lagos?

The Development Levy applies to our assessable profits. As a resident company, we'd need to calculate our assessable profits to see if the 4% levy applies. Small companies and non-resident companies are exempt, but this depends on our specific circumstances - we'd need to confirm our company status and tax obligations. Please confirm our company specifics with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant to accurately determine our Development Levy liability and ensure all tax requirements are met.
I own a small electronics shop in Kano, how do I know if my business is considered a 'small company' for tax exemption?

Under the new rules, your business is expected to be considered 'small' if it has an annual gross turnover of NGN 100 million or below and total fixed assets of NGN 250 million or below. If your shop meets both of these conditions, it's likely to be exempt from certain taxes. Please confirm with FIRS or a licensed accountant to ensure you meet the specific requirements.
What personal income tax bands should I expect as the owner of the furniture workshop in Ibadan, and is there any tax-free threshold?

The tax bands are progressive, meaning they go up by different percentages, from 0% to 25%. Individuals earning below NGN 800,000 per year are exempt from paying personal income tax. However, this is expected to be the case as per the new tax rules, so it's always best to check with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant to confirm specifics before filing.

If your business has been running for more than 18 months, you need to file within 6 months after the end of your accounting year. If you're a new company, you have 18 months from when you were incorporated, or 6 months after the end of your first accounting period, whichever comes first. If you're closing down, you have 6 months from when you stopped trading. Remember to confirm these details with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
I send money to my family in Nigeria from time to time, but I'm not living there or doing business. Do I need a TIN?

Under the new tax reforms, you're only expected to obtain a TIN if you or your family have taxable income or business activities in Nigeria. If your money transfers are just for personal or family use and don't generate income, it's unlikely you'll need to register for a TIN. However, to be certain, please confirm with the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before making any official declarations.
I send money back to my family in Nigeria every month, will that be taxed?

Under the new rules, this is expected to not be considered taxable income, as genuine personal remittances for family support are not subject to tax. To confirm specifics, it's best to check with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
Do I need a TIN for my agro-input dealer in Kano, and how do I get one?

As an agro-input dealer in Kano, under the new reform rules, you only need a TIN if you're earning taxable income or have business activities in Nigeria. If your business is already registered, you should already have a TIN, and it's linked to your Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) registration. If not, you can apply for a TIN through the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) / Nigeria Revenue Service or you may use your National Identification Number (NIN) if you're an individual business owner. Please note to confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing, as tax regulations can change.

Additionally, if you're awarded a contract and you're not registered, the company that awarded the contract will also face a penalty. Please confirm these details with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure you're meeting all tax obligations.
What are the personal income tax bands and rent relief rules for the owner?

The new tax reform applies a progressive income tax system from 0% to 25% for the owner. However, individuals earning below NGN 800,000 per annum are expected to be exempt from paying personal income tax under these new rules.

Before filing your taxes, please confirm these specifics with the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant to ensure compliance with the new rules.

To confirm specifics, it's best to check with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.

To determine if your business owes this levy, you'll need to check if you're a 'small company' and/or a 'non-resident company'. If not, you'll likely need to pay the Development Levy.

You'll want to confirm specifics with FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing to ensure you're meeting all the necessary requirements accurately.

Based on the Nigeria Tax Reform Acts 2026, if your electronics retailer business meets the 'small company definition' (both annual gross turnover and total fixed assets are below NGN 100,000,000 and NGN 250,000,000 respectively), then you are exempt from paying Companies Income Tax.

However, for most small businesses in Nigeria, the Companies Income Tax rate under the new Act is 0% (no tax to pay).

It's crucial to confirm your business specifics regarding the tax-exempt status, as you must verify these details with the Nigeria Revenue Service (FIRS) or consult a licensed accountant before filing to ensure accuracy.

Under the new rules, your business is expected to be considered a 'small company' if it has an annual gross turnover of NGN 100 million or below and total fixed assets of NGN 250 million or below. If your business meets both these conditions, it is expected to be exempt from certain taxes. Please confirm these details with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.

Under the Nigeria Tax Reform Act (effective 2026), income earned entirely outside Nigeria by a non-resident is expected to be exempt from Nigerian tax, even if paid into a Nigerian account. However, to confirm this applies to your specific situation, you should consult FIRS/the Nigeria Revenue Service or a licensed accountant before filing your tax returns.

Additionally, if you're awarded a contract by a statutory body or company while unregistered, they'll also be liable to a penalty. Always confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant before filing.
As an agro-input dealer in Abuja, do we need to pay Companies Income Tax?

Based on the new Nigeria Tax Reform Acts 2025, if your agro-input company's annual gross turnover is below NGN 100 million and total fixed assets are below NGN 250 million, you might be considered a 'small company'. As per Section 56/57 of the new NTA, a small company is exempt from paying Companies Income Tax. However, I would advise that you confirm this with a licensed accountant or the Nigeria Revenue Service to ensure our company meets all the necessary conditions before filing.
